title: Rotate the laptop display with the accelerometer on convertibles
head: 7fd833606f44
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
decision: Two visible findings (ISO package list, panel mode/position overwritten); More findings: touch/pen, reload undoes lock, base-only accelerometers, claim held while panel off; related PRs #7493/#9160/#13148/#7000 in Details.

leads.summary: Detector excludes sensor types supported by the shipped iio-sensor-proxy
leads.consequence: A supported buffered IIO accelerometer can expose scan_elements/in_accel_{x,y,z}_en without in_accel_x_raw, and an input/event accelerometer is not under /sys/bus/iio at all. Both return false: fresh installs skip the package, existing installs mark the migration complete without installing it, the autostart daemon exits, and the menu hides Auto-rotate. The user sees no feature or setup error even though iio-sensor-proxy supports the device. Match the proxy's actual supported sensor types or its HasAccelerometer property where available, with a plan for before-package installation.

leads.summary: Add iio-sensor-proxy to the ISO offline package mirror list
leads.consequence: The new hardware installer invokes omarchy-pkg-add iio-sensor-proxy at ISO finalization, but neither package list supplying the ISO's offline mirror names the package. An offline installation on a detected convertible has no package to satisfy pacman -S; pkg-add exits 1 and run_logged reports failure to the installer, so installation can stop instead of just omitting rotation. Add iio-sensor-proxy to install/omarchy-other.packages (as related PRs #7493 and #13148 independently do).

leads.summary: An IIO raw accelerometer in the laptop base passes the display-sensor guard
leads.consequence: The proxy distinguishes base from display/lid accelerometers and ignores the former for orientation. With only an IIO base sensor that exposes in_accel_x_raw, this detector still installs the package, displays Auto-rotate and starts a permanent monitor-sensor/socat process, while HasAccelerometer is false and no orientation ever arrives. The menu can claim rotation was enabled though the panel cannot rotate. Use the same location filtering or the proxy's HasAccelerometer check for the runtime UI and daemon (and don't assume x_raw alone is sufficient).

leads.summary: Coordinate competing open PR #7493 before merging this feature
leads.consequence: #7493 is diverged, not stacked, and adds different content under the *same new hardware-detector and installer paths*, plus its own auto-rotation daemon, autostart and menu entry. A three-way merge using its merge-base generates add/add conflicts for those new files and adjacent-hunk conflicts in autostart and menu. Blindly keeping both daemons yields two sensor claimants and competing writes to the built-in output, with independent rotate-lock/autorotate-off toggles. Choose one owner for auto-rotation, unify hardware detection and tests, and resolve overlapping registrations rather than merging either blindly.

leads.summary: Related GPD Pocket 4 PR #9160 adds a second live rotation owner
leads.consequence: #9160 enables a GPD-specific user service on the same machine; it claims the same sensor and writes hl.monitor on the same built-in eDP while also transforming touch. This PR unconditionally starts another watcher on detected hardware. With both PRs merged, turning this PR's rotation lock on does not lock the GPD service, and a user-configured GPD orientation offset can be overwritten by this PR's unoffset transform. The two independently set panel rules (and only one sets touch) depending on event order. Exclude the GPD service's machine from the generic daemon, or integrate with one rotation owner and one lock.

leads.summary: Rotation lock does not survive a Hyprland config reload
leads.consequence: If the panel was rotated when autorotate-off was set, a config reload restores the unrotated configured rule. The reload listener reads the saved orientation, but apply_orientation sees the lock and returns without reapplying the frozen transform; the locked display visibly rotates back until unlocked or manually rotated. Preserve the locked panel transform across reloads, distinct from suppressing new sensor orientation changes.

leads.summary: Do not keep the accelerometer claimed when the built-in panel is off
leads.consequence: Once the machine has a raw IIO sensor, this always-on startup loop holds monitor-sensor open while docked with the lid closed or the internal screen manually disabled, even though apply_transform finds no active built-in panel and skips. The upstream sensor-proxy contract explicitly recommends releasing the claim when the main screen is off to avoid unnecessary polling, wake-ups and battery use. Tie the claim to an active built-in output or stop monitoring while the panel is disabled and resume on enable.

leads.summary: Respect the monitor-management opt-out introduced by open PR #7000
leads.consequence: #7000's monitor-management off option is meant to hand automatic monitor handling to another manager; it guards the existing monitor watcher, clamshell and manual/internal paths, but this new unconditional daemon never checks that flag. If both merge, a sensor event still changes the internal monitor's mode/position/transform while automatic management is off. Add the same guard to the new daemon and its unlock/apply path, or explicitly distinguish/document user opt-outs so an external manager can own the panel.

leads.summary: Add the new hardware toggle to the sibling toggle documentation
leads.consequence: This manual's toggle table lists the hardware-menu touchpad, touchscreen and hybrid GPU commands but not omarchy toggle autorotate. Users looking up hardware toggles from the toggle documentation will not find the new command or learn that its menu entry lives under Trigger > Hardware. Add a row and qualify the menu placement alongside the other conditional hardware switches.

leads.summary: Rotate a built-in touchscreen's calibration alongside the panel
leads.consequence: On a convertible with a built-in touchscreen that supports libinput calibration, changing only hl.monitor.transform does not update the touch device's transform. Hyprland v0.56.2 reads touchdevice:transform separately and applies a libinput calibration matrix, then maps touch positions on the monitor. In portrait, taps can land away from the finger until the touch device is transformed as well. Bind and transform only the touchscreen associated with the built-in output, and restore it on reload; do not blindly rotate external touch devices.

leads.summary: Add coverage for detector, daemon, and lock rather than relying on generic metadata tests
leads.consequence: No test exercises any new autorotate script or migration. A plausible regression, detecting only x_raw and silently excluding valid buffered/input sensors, passes the existing all-bin metadata and generic menu tests. A second plausible regression, treating reload as a new locked orientation and skipping frozen-transform reapply, also passes. Add stubbed sensor/Hyprland fixtures asserting these cases and a migration/package-list fixture; follow the existing monitor-test.sh and menu-test.sh style.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Offline ISO installs halt on accelerometer machines.

### iio-sensor-proxy is missing from the ISO package lists

`install/hardware/accelerometer.sh` installs it, but the ISO's offline mirror is built from the `install/omarchy-*.packages` lists and lacks it. **Impact:** pacman fails with "target not found" and the install halts.

**Suggested change:** add `iio-sensor-proxy` to `install/omarchy-other.packages`, as #7493 and #13148 do.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 7fd83360)</summary>

# iio-sensor-proxy is missing from the ISO package lists

The ISO builds its offline mirror from install/omarchy-base.packages and install/omarchy-other.packages (plus dependencies), and the target's pacman.conf points only at that mirror while omarchy-apply-hardware runs. install/hardware/accelerometer.sh installs iio-sensor-proxy, which is in neither list.

Save as `test/shell.d/accelerometer-offline-package-test.sh` in a checkout of the PR head (7fd83360) and run it:

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

# The ISO builds its offline mirror from these two lists (plus dependencies), and
# the target's pacman.conf points only at that mirror while omarchy-apply-hardware
# runs. A package a hardware leaf installs has to be listed, or pacman reports
# "target not found" and the hardware step stops the install.
for pkg in $(sed -nE 's/^[[:space:]]*omarchy-pkg-add[[:space:]]+//p' "$ROOT/install/hardware/accelerometer.sh"); do
  grep -qx -- "$pkg" "$ROOT/install/omarchy-base.packages" "$ROOT/install/omarchy-other.packages" ||
    fail "$pkg from install/hardware/accelerometer.sh is in the ISO package lists"
done
pass "accelerometer packages are in the ISO package lists"
```

Actual output at 7fd83360 (exit status 1). The first line is the command; everything after it is the test's own output, captured unchanged from a sandboxed run against a copy of `bin/`, `install/`, `migrations/` and `test/shell.d/base-test.sh` at that commit:

```text
$ bash test/shell.d/accelerometer-offline-package-test.sh
not ok - iio-sensor-proxy from install/hardware/accelerometer.sh is in the ISO package lists
```

With `iio-sensor-proxy` appended to `install/omarchy-other.packages` the same test prints `ok - accelerometer packages are in the ISO package lists` and exits 0.
</details>

### Panel mode and position are overwritten at login and reload

At session start (even upright) and on each unlocked reload, the daemon writes a rule with `mode = "preferred", position = "auto"`. **Impact:** per Hyprland 0.56.2 source, a user's `eDP-1` mode and position are replaced, and a `desc:` panel rule stops applying.

**Suggested change:** carry the live mode and position with the scale; skipping upright writes is only partial.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 7fd83360)</summary>

# An unrotated panel loses its configured mode and position

monitor-sensor reports the starting orientation at every session start. The daemon answers it with a monitor rule that hard-codes mode "preferred" and position "auto", even when the device is held normally and the panel is placed and clocked by the user's monitors.lua.

Save as `test/shell.d/autorotate-panel-rule-test.sh` in a checkout of the PR head (7fd83360) and run it:

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

test_dir=$(mktemp -d)
stub_bin="$test_dir/bin"
eval_log="$test_dir/eval.log"
pids="$test_dir/pids"
mkdir -p "$stub_bin" "$test_dir/runtime"
daemon_pid=""

cleanup() {
  if [[ -n $daemon_pid ]]; then
    kill "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  if [[ -f $pids ]]; then
    while read -r pid; do kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true; done <"$pids"
  fi
  rm -rf "$test_dir"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

# A convertible docked under a 1440p screen, its panel placed at 0x1440 and run
# at 120 Hz by the user's monitors.lua. hyprctl reports those live values.
cat >"$test_dir/monitors.json" <<'EOF'
[
  {"name":"DP-1","width":2560,"height":1440,"refreshRate":144.0,"x":0,"y":0,"scale":1,"transform":0},
  {"name":"eDP-1","width":2880,"height":1800,"refreshRate":120.0,"x":0,"y":1440,"scale":1.6,"transform":0}
]
EOF

cat >"$stub_bin/hyprctl" <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
case "\$1" in
  monitors) cat "$test_dir/monitors.json" ;;
  eval) printf '%s\n' "\$2" >>"$eval_log" ;;
esac
EOF

# The device is held normally. monitor-sensor reports that once, as it does
# every time the session starts, and then waits for a change that never comes.
cat >"$stub_bin/monitor-sensor" <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
echo \$\$ >>"$pids"
echo "=== Has accelerometer (orientation: normal, tilt: tilted-down)"
exec sleep 30
EOF

cat >"$stub_bin/socat" <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
echo \$\$ >>"$pids"
exec sleep 30
EOF

printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$stub_bin/omarchy-hw-accelerometer"
chmod +x "$stub_bin"/*

HOME="$test_dir" XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$test_dir/runtime" HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE=test PATH="$stub_bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" \
  "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-hyprland-monitor-autorotate" >/dev/null &
daemon_pid=$!

for _ in {1..60}; do
  [[ -s $eval_log ]] && break
  sleep 0.05
done

kill -0 "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || fail "the autorotate daemon is running"

rule=$(cat "$eval_log" 2>/dev/null || true)
[[ $rule != *'mode = "preferred"'* && $rule != *'position = "auto"'* ]] ||
  fail "an unrotated panel keeps its mode and position" "hyprctl eval $rule"
pass "an unrotated panel keeps its mode and position"
```

Actual output at 7fd83360 (exit status 1). The first line is the command; everything after it is the test's own output, captured unchanged from a sandboxed run against a copy of `bin/`, `install/`, `migrations/` and `test/shell.d/base-test.sh` at that commit:

```text
$ bash test/shell.d/autorotate-panel-rule-test.sh
hyprctl eval hl.monitor({ output = "eDP-1", mode = "preferred", position = "auto", scale = 1.6, transform = 0 })
not ok - an unrotated panel keeps its mode and position
```

With a diagnostic change that writes the live `WxH@Hz` mode and `XxY` position instead, the same test prints `ok - an unrotated panel keeps its mode and position` and exits 0. The test also passes if no rule is written at all while the panel is already upright.
</details>

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

#### Touch and pen input are not rotated

Not reproduced; from Hyprland 0.56.2 source. Touch and tablet input are mapped without the monitor's transform, so after the daemon rotates the panel they still report in the panel's native orientation. **Impact:** in portrait or upside down, taps and pen strokes likely land in the wrong place. **Suggested change:** also set the transform of the built-in touch and tablet devices (for example with `hl.device({ name = ..., transform = N })`), as #9160 does for its touchscreen.

#### A config reload undoes the rotation lock

Every reload drops the rule written by `hyprctl eval`, so the panel returns to the transform in `monitors.lua` (none). `watch_reloads` re-applies through `apply_orientation`, which returns early while `autorotate-off` is set. **Impact:** a panel locked in portrait snaps back to landscape on the next reload (toggles, lid and clamshell switching, config edits), although `manual/33-monitors.md` says the screen stays where it was. **Suggested change:** record the transform in force when the lock is taken, and re-apply it on `configreloaded` while the lock holds.

The lock-and-reload reproducer follows this block.

#### Base-only accelerometers enable the feature on clamshell laptops

Not reproduced on hardware; from source and a sandboxed detector run. `omarchy-hw-accelerometer` only checks for `in_accel_x_raw`, but iio-sensor-proxy ignores accelerometers located in the base and reports `HasAccelerometer` false for them. systemd's `60-sensor.hwdb` marks the sensor-hub accelerometer as `ACCEL_LOCATION=base` on over twenty Dell Latitude, Precision and Vostro SKUs. **Impact:** those laptops get `iio-sensor-proxy` (and the offline install failure above if the live environment exposes the sensor), an Auto-rotate menu entry that does nothing, and a daemon that never rotates. **Suggested change:** skip devices whose `label` is `accel-base` or whose udev `ACCEL_LOCATION` is `base`, or gate the menu and daemon on the proxy's `HasAccelerometer`.

#### The sensor stays claimed while the built-in panel is off

From source and stub runs. `monitor-sensor` keeps its claim for the whole session, including while docked with the lid closed or with the panel disabled. `net.hadess.SensorProxy.xml` asks clients to release the claim when the main screen is off, because a held claim keeps the proxy polling the sensor. **Impact:** while docked with the lid closed, the proxy keeps polling a sensor whose readings are never used, adding wake-ups that the interface docs say reduce battery life. **Suggested change:** stop `monitor-sensor` while the built-in panel is disabled and start it again when the panel returns.
</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: lock and reload (fails at 7fd83360)</summary>

# A config reload undoes the rotation lock

Hyprland drops rules added by hyprctl eval on every reload, so the panel returns to the transform monitors.lua gives it (none). The daemon re-applies the orientation on configreloaded, but not while the lock is on, so a locked portrait panel goes back to landscape on the next reload.

Save as `test/shell.d/autorotate-lock-reload-test.sh` in a checkout of the PR head (7fd83360) and run it:

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

test_dir=$(mktemp -d)
stub_bin="$test_dir/bin"
eval_log="$test_dir/eval.log"
pids="$test_dir/pids"
state="$test_dir/runtime/omarchy-monitor-autorotate.orientation"
lock="$test_dir/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/autorotate-off"
mkdir -p "$stub_bin" "$test_dir/runtime"
daemon_pid=""

stop_daemon() {
  if [[ -n $daemon_pid ]]; then
    kill "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  daemon_pid=""
  if [[ -f $pids ]]; then
    while read -r pid; do kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true; done <"$pids"
  fi
  rm -f "$pids"
}
trap 'stop_daemon; rm -rf "$test_dir"' EXIT

cat >"$test_dir/monitors.json" <<'EOF'
[{"name":"eDP-1","width":2880,"height":1800,"refreshRate":120.0,"x":0,"y":0,"scale":2,"transform":1}]
EOF

cat >"$stub_bin/hyprctl" <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
case "\$1" in
  monitors) cat "$test_dir/monitors.json" ;;
  eval) printf '%s\n' "\$2" >>"$eval_log" ;;
esac
EOF

# Hyprland reloads its config (a theme change, a toggle, the lid), which puts the
# panel back to the transform monitors.lua gives it: none.
cat >"$stub_bin/socat" <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
echo \$\$ >>"$pids"
echo "configreloaded>>"
exec sleep 30
EOF

# The device does not move while this runs.
cat >"$stub_bin/monitor-sensor" <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
echo \$\$ >>"$pids"
exec sleep 30
EOF

printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$stub_bin/omarchy-hw-accelerometer"
chmod +x "$stub_bin"/*

reload_rule() {
  rm -f "$eval_log"
  HOME="$test_dir" XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$test_dir/runtime" HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE=test PATH="$stub_bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" \
    "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-hyprland-monitor-autorotate" >/dev/null &
  daemon_pid=$!
  for _ in {1..40}; do
    [[ -s $eval_log ]] && break
    sleep 0.05
  done
  stop_daemon
  cat "$eval_log" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Portrait, rotation on: the reload is undone.
printf 'left-up\n' >"$state"
rule=$(reload_rule)
[[ $rule == *"transform = 1 })" ]] || fail "a reload keeps a rotated panel rotated" "$rule"
pass "a reload keeps a rotated panel rotated"

# Portrait, then the lock: the manual promises the screen stays where it was.
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$lock")"
touch "$lock"
rule=$(reload_rule)
[[ $rule == *"transform = 1 })" ]] || fail "a reload keeps a locked panel where the lock left it" "no hyprctl eval after configreloaded"
pass "a reload keeps a locked panel where the lock left it"
```

Actual output at 7fd83360 (exit status 1). The first line is the command; everything after it is the test's own output, captured unchanged from a sandboxed run against a copy of `bin/`, `install/`, `migrations/` and `test/shell.d/base-test.sh` at that commit:

```text
$ bash test/shell.d/autorotate-lock-reload-test.sh
ok - a reload keeps a rotated panel rotated
no hyprctl eval after configreloaded
not ok - a reload keeps a locked panel where the lock left it
```

With a diagnostic change that re-applies the recorded transform on configreloaded regardless of the lock, both checks print `ok` and the test exits 0.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Related open PRs**
- #7493 implements the same feature and adds the same new paths (`bin/omarchy-hw-accelerometer`, `install/hardware/accelerometer.sh`) with different content, so the two conflict as they stand.
- #9160 adds a GPD Pocket 4 rotation service that also writes `eDP-1` rules from the same sensor; with both merged, that device would likely have two rotators.
- #13148 also installs `iio-sensor-proxy`, from a different hardware script.
- #7000 (open) adds a `monitor-management` toggle and makes the monitor scripts check it; if both land, this daemon needs the same check.

**Verified** (source reading and sandboxed runs)
- Orientation mapping `normal`/`left-up`/`bottom-up`/`right-up` to transforms 0/1/2/3, matching mutter and iio-hyprland.
- Every `monitor-sensor` 3.9 message form is parsed, and tilt and `undefined` lines are ignored.
- External monitors and a disabled built-in panel get no rule.
- The toggle locks, then unlocks and catches up to the current orientation; `omarchy toggle autorotate` reaches it.
- Without an accelerometer the daemon exits at once; the existing test suites give identical results at the base and head.

**Optional:** `manual/13-toggles-idle-screensaver.md` lists the other _Trigger > Hardware_ toggles (touchpad, touchscreen, hybrid GPU) but not `omarchy toggle autorotate`.
</details>
